summary.text: Julian Villarreal is the Green Party candidate for the Texas State Senate, District 26, in the November 3, 2026 general election, challenging Democratic incumbent José Menéndez.
He is a scientific consultant and former university lecturer who also ran for the seat in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Julian Villarreal was born in San Antonio, Texas, and graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology with a bachelor's degree in 2007.

His professional experience includes working as a scientific consultant and as a lecturer in physics and researcher at the University of Texas at San Antonio, and he has been affiliated with the Bexar County Green Party and Climate Action SA.

In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Villarreal said he holds a PhD in materials science and engineering from the University of Texas at Austin and serves as an election judge and volunteer deputy registrar in Bexar County.
Villarreal ran in the November 3, 2020 general election for Texas Senate District 26, which incumbent José Menéndez won.
He advanced from the Green Party convention on March 14, 2026.
In his 2020 survey, he said he was running to give voters a progressive choice and raise issues such as climate change, and that he does not accept contributions from corporate PACs or lobbyists.
